terms.grammar: verb, third conjugation; in + accusative; sē vertere, to turn oneself into
evidence: Plaut. Am. prol. 121: Juppiter in Amphitruōnis vortit sēsē imāginem (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: To turn something into something else, in with the accusative (Lewis & Short).

evidence: Ov. M. 1.88: tellūs induit ignōtās hominum conversa figūrās (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: First to turn round; then to change the nature of a thing (Lewis & Short).

terms.register: vōx plērumque poētica: Verg., Ov.; then post-Augustan prose
evidence: Verg. G. 4.441: omnia trānsfōrmat sēsē in mīrācula rērum (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Change of outward shape, as in Ovid’s tales; Quintilian uses it of the mind taking on the nature of its subject (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: Juppiter in Amphitruōnis vortit sēsē imāginem
phrases.english: Jupiter turns himself into the likeness of Amphitryon

phrases.latin: omnia trānsfōrmat sēsē in mīrācula rērum
phrases.english: he turns himself into every wonder in the world

sources: Lewis & Short: verto · Lewis & Short: converto · Lewis & Short: transformo
